description:
Split out of fz-5xp.14 with authorization (user, 2026-09-07: 'we can skip them
for the moment').

`String.splitter/3` is `split/3` that yields parts lazily instead of building
the whole list, and in Elixir it returns a Stream. fz has no Stream and no lazy
enumerable of any kind.

Everything else in fz-5xp.14's class D shipped; this is the only one that needs
a capability rather than code.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: fz's Enumerable already has the SUSPEND half of the reduce
protocol -- `{:suspend, acc}` and the `{:suspended, acc, continuation}` reply
are implemented in enum.fz and list.fz -- which is exactly the machinery a
Stream is built on. So this is closer than it looks: what is missing is a Stream
module that packages a suspendable reduce as a value, not the suspension
mechanism itself.

Related: several Enum functions would become lazy the same way, and
fz-5xp.16's remaining audit item about the fifth Enumerable callback
(reduce_while/3) bears on what a Stream would have to implement.
title: String.splitter/3 needs a Stream
